title: Finite coefficient completed pullback square with its actual units
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $E\subset L$ finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $A_F=\mathcal O_F$ and chosen uniformizers $t_F$ for $F=E,L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On its small pro-etale site put $B_{F,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A_F/t_F^n)_X$ and $F_X=B_{F,X}[1/t_F]$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use sheaves of modules, sheaf tensor products and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_F(X)=D^b_c(X,A_F)$ for the completed integral category with compatible etale-origin witnesses, $Q_F:\mathcal C_F(X)\to\mathcal R_F(X)=\mathcal C_F(X)[1/t_F]$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, def-weil-pbc-rational-category], and $J_{F,X}(Q_FK)=F_X\otimes^L_{B_{F,X}}K$, $J_{F,X}(f/t_F^n)=t_F^{-n}(F_X\otimes^L f)$ [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Let $C_X=B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}-$, with constructible restriction and raw rationalization $T_{L/E,X}$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Let $g:X'\to X$ be a scheme map with $X'$ satisfying the same hypotheses and define the coefficient sheaves on $X'$ in the same way. The coefficient maps $c_{F,g}$ are defined by their finite quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Put $P_{F,g}=B_{F,X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}B_{F,X}}g^{-1}(-)$, and let $\widehat P_{F,g}$ and $\gamma_{F,g}:P_{F,g}\to\widehat P_{F,g}$ be precisely quotient-tower completed pullback and its specified unit [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For $W=X,X'$ write $\Lambda_{F,W}$ for local derived $t_F$-completion with unit $\eta_{F,W}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], identified with quotient completion including units [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

The sheaf $B_{L,W}$ is finite free of rank $[L:E]$ over $B_{E,W}$, and $t_E=ut_L^e$ for a unit $u$ and $e\geq1$, without any unramified assumption [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There is a natural isomorphism on all ambient complexes
$$\kappa_W:C_W\Lambda_{E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{L,W}C_W,\qquad \kappa_{W,N}C_W(\eta_{E,W,N})=\eta_{L,W,C_WN}.$$
It is the identity-coefficient unitor and commutes with every successive finite coefficient associator, including positive ramification indices.

The finite-projection coefficient square yields the ordinary balanced comparison $\beta_g:C_{X'}P_{E,g}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{L,g}C_X$. On flat-term K-flat representatives both sides flatten to $B_{L,X'}\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{E,X}}g^{-1}P$, and $s'\otimes r'\otimes p$ maps to $s'i_{X'}(r')\otimes p$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. With the canonical derived adjunctions, the right adjoints preserve local complete objects and have the unit-normalized direct-image/completion comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pushforward-completion]. In the reflected coefficient-square construction [lem-weil-pbc-reflected-adjunction-coefficient-squares], the data are $F_0=P_{E,g}$, $F_1=P_{L,g}$, $C_A=C_X$, $C_B=C_{X'}$, $\delta=\beta_g^{-1}$ and the displayed $\kappa$'s. Its inverse comparison is
$$\widehat\beta_{g,K}=\Lambda_{L,X'}(\beta_{g,K})\kappa_{X',P_{E,g}K}:C_{X'}\widehat P_{E,g}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat P_{L,g}C_XK.$$
This is the specific finite-quotient-normalized scalar/pullback comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and it satisfies the actual unit equation
$$\widehat\beta_{g,K}C_{X'}(\gamma_{E,g,K})=\gamma_{L,g,C_XK}\beta_{g,K}.$$
The intermediate expression for either side is $\Lambda_{L,X'}(\beta_{g,K})\eta_{L,X',C_{X'}P_{E,g}K}$. The equation identifies the finite quotient completion units, rather than only the objects up to isomorphism. On $K\in\mathcal C_E(X)$ both $\gamma$'s are isomorphisms, and $C_XK\in\mathcal C_L(X)$ [lem-per-rational-realization-pullback-comparison, prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. These comparisons obey identity, geometric composition and coefficient-tower pasting with the ambient pullback comparators and the specified raw scalar associators.

proof.text: Construct the ambient strict-tower comparison by conjugating stratumReductionIso with the specified ordinary and tower transports. Its augmentation equation is reductionAugmentationTransport. Apply derived limit, the constant/limit unit equation, and actualCompletion_quotient. The resulting natural isomorphism preserves the actual unit on every ambient object. For uniqueness, cancel its inverse and apply the injective reflector Hom map into the intrinsically complete output; no completeness hypothesis on the input is used.

Transport the finite-free completed coefficient module of finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison along the projection-normalized coefficient presentation isomorphisms. coefficientScalar_square identifies the actual scalar action; identity-on-sections restriction composition, the regular-module isomorphism, and preservation of finite products transport the basis with its unchanged relative degree. integral_ramification gives the unit times a positive power factorization in the valuation rings. Lift its unit through ULift and apply the completed-section ring homomorphisms; scalarCompletedCoefficientSection identifies the coefficient images.

The specified pbcScalarCompletionIso is chosen from its unique unit-normalized existence theorem. Compose its unit equation with its inverse to obtain the kappa unit equation. The reflected comparison is definitionally kappa followed by completion of ordinary beta. Expand the conjugated strict comparison, cancel the target ambient comparison with its inverse, combine the two source scalar maps, and use the source ambient unit equation. Substitution of the kappa unit equation gives the common intermediate expression. Naturality of the target completion unit and cancellation of the target ambient comparison prove the strict unit square.

For constructible input, pbcEmbeddingAmbientTensor_preserves supplies all three scalar-extended membership conditions. Choose the existing rational realization data on both schemes for E and L, and apply rationalRealizationPullbackComparison at each field. Its integral.unit_isIso fields give exactly the two specified strict-unit isomorphisms.

Use pbcActualDirectCompletionIso_exists and its chosen comparison unit equation. A complete input has invertible completion unit; direct image preserves that isomorphism, so the comparison equation and its invertible component imply that the completion unit on the direct image is invertible. Intrinsic completeness is invariant under isomorphism, and the reflected object is intrinsically complete. This proves preservation and the specified right-adjoint normalization.

The existing pbcScalarCompletedPull_identity, pbcScalarCompletedPull_comp, pbcScalarCompletion_coefficients and pbcScalarCompletedPull_coefficients prove the stated pasting equations verbatim. For identity coefficients, cancel the tensor unitor, then apply the injectivity of precomposition with the reflection unit. Naturality of the inverse tensor unitor, the kappa unit equation, and naturality of the completion unit identify the two maps. Thus the specified kappa has precisely the tensor-unitor formula.

The ordinary module comparison is the inverse conjugate of the identity-on-sections right-adjoint comparison. Evaluate the conjugate-unit equation on a section. The normalized scalar and geometric adjunction units give the beta formula for tensor coefficient one. The scalar adjunction unit is linear, and the ordinary comparison is linear; the scalar pure tensor is s times its coefficient-one tensor. These identities give s tensor (r times the pullback generator) mapping to s times i(r) times the target generator. The derived representative equation is exactly the normalization of pbcActualScalarDerivedPullIso_exists, unfolded through pbcScalarOrdinaryPullIso and inverse beta.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q79-9c63b0df4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item's statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the Q151 base copy. There are no new nodes and no repair note. I read seven steps against the full statements of all 13 cited nodes, the full statement of prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension and its proof steps 5-7 and 9. I also read Stacks 0A0G, 0A0E, 099J, 099B, 0G7E, 07A4 and 0D6D, whose labels match the tags file. Step 1: uniqueness of the extended absolute value plus DVR clause 5 give t_E = u t_L^e, and |t_E|_L < 1 forces e >= 1, so ramification is not restricted. Step 2: the finite-free completion transport hypotheses hold, and the Noetherian hypothesis of the constant-completion equivalence holds (O_E with ideal (t_E)). Step 3: the coefficient square commutes on finite projections because t_E^n is in (t_L^n). So both composite ringed morphisms are equal, and the c_{f,g} of the ringed monoidal comparisons give beta_g; that node needs no flatness. Step 4: the generated ideal is (t_F), so pushforward-completion gives gamma with gamma eta = G(eta). The Čech-model and Koszul reflectors agree by the unique unit-compatible isomorphism, an elementary step. delta = beta^{-1} is in the right direction, and the inverse of delta-hat is Lambda(beta)kappa. Step 5: Lambda(beta)kappa C(eta_E) = Lambda(beta)eta = eta beta follows from kappa's unit equation and naturality of eta; this is elementary and correct. Step 6: constructible scalar transport puts C_X K in the L-category, and the realization/pullback comparison applied at E and at L makes gamma an isomorphism for any g. Step 7: pasting follows from the statements of reflected squares, monoidal comparisons and the transport tower law. Edge cases checked: empty X, g = id, E = L, e > 1, K = 0. Batch-5: lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective, reached only through ring-isomorphism tensor transport, is a Mathlib leaf: essential surjectivity of a localization functor, a general category fact outside both assumptions and not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so I accept it. All 11 declared tool_uses are generic black boxes and I accept them. Maintainer note: prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension's statement only asserts that coherent comparisons exist. Its proof step 6 builds the inverse of Lambda(beta)kappa, so it agrees with this item's beta-hat, but the proposition's statement could pin it. No changes.
